basic_information.name: Lindy AI
basic_information.creator: Lindy AI Inc. (founded by Flo Crivello, former Uber engineer and PM; headquartered in San Francisco, CA). Pivoted from TeamFlow (a virtual office startup that raised $50M) to Lindy after identifying the AI agent automation opportunity in 2022-2023.
basic_information.description: Lindy AI is a no-code AI agent platform that lets anyone build and deploy autonomous AI workers to automate complex business workflows without programming. Unlike traditional automation tools like Zapier that use rigid if-then rules, Lindy leverages large language models to create agents that understand context, make decisions, and adapt to changing situations. The platform combines three core capabilities: Agent Builder (natural language agent creation), Computer Use (browser automation for apps without APIs), and AI Phone Agents (Gaia) for voice interactions. For entrepreneurs, Lindy provides a fast path to automating knowledge work such as email triage, lead qualification, customer support, meeting notes, and CRM updates, with 4,000+ integrations and a free tier to validate use cases before scaling.
basic_information.release_date: March 2023 (initial launch with waitlist; 70,000 signups from demo video). Lindy 3.0 launched August 2025 with Agent Builder, Computer Use, and Team Accounts.

technical_capabilities.underlying_models: Multi-provider: Claude Sonnet 4.5 (default, best for coding with 77.2% SWE-bench score), Claude Sonnet 3.7, Claude Haiku 3.5, GPT-5, GPT-5 Codex, and Gemini Flash 2.0. Users can select models per agent. Lindy positions Claude Sonnet 4.5 as the default for best overall performance.
technical_capabilities.customization_depth: workflow-builder | code-extension. Lindy provides a visual workflow builder with drag-and-drop triggers, conditions, and actions. Users can define agent behavior through natural language prompts. Advanced customization via HTTP Request actions for arbitrary API calls with custom methods, headers, and JSON bodies. Computer Use extends automation to any web application without APIs.
technical_capabilities.api_access: Yes. REST API for programmatic use, webhook triggers with unique URLs and security settings for custom automations, HTTP fetch capabilities for custom API connections, and Lindy Embed for deploying agents as chat widgets or iFrames.
technical_capabilities.deployment_options: Cloud-hosted (primary), embeddable web chat widget (popup or iFrame modes via Lindy Embed), website integration (Squarespace, WordPress via code injection), phone agent deployment (inbound and outbound calls via Gaia), email/SMS channels. No self-hosted or on-device option.
technical_capabilities.ai_model_flexibility: multi-provider. Supports models from Anthropic (Claude family), OpenAI (GPT-5), and Google (Gemini Flash). Users can choose models per agent. No explicit bring-your-own-model option documented for standard plans; Enterprise plan may offer custom model integration.

user_experience.target_user: business_user | marketer | enterprise_team | student. Lindy targets non-technical business users who want to automate knowledge work. Described as the 'Zapier of AI,' it bridges the gap between simple automation tools and developer-centric frameworks. Strong fit for sales teams, customer support, operations, and solopreneurs.
user_experience.learning_curve: minutes. Lindy emphasizes going from prompt to production agent in 60 seconds. Basic agent creation is achievable in under 5 minutes with the Getting Started 101 tutorial. Advanced multi-step workflows with integrations take hours.
user_experience.setup_time: 5-10 minutes from signup to first working AI email assistant using templates
user_experience.collaboration_features: Team Accounts introduced in Lindy 3.0 (August 2025) for sharing AI agents across departments. Team members can be added for $19.99/month each on Pro and Business plans. Enterprise plans include dedicated team management features.
user_experience.template_library: Extensive template library with 1,000+ pre-built templates covering sales, support, meetings, email, medical scribes, podcast notetakers, meeting recorders, and dozens of other practical use cases. Templates can be copied to your account and started immediately. Categories include Outbound Sales, Customer Support Triage, CRM automation, and more.
user_experience.visual_builder_type: hybrid. Combines natural-language agent creation (describe what you want in plain English) with a visual workflow builder (drag-and-drop triggers, conditions, and actions). Users can switch between prompt-based configuration and visual flow editing.

ai_and_rag_capabilities.rag_support: Built-in knowledge base with RAG pipeline. Free tier includes 1M character knowledge base, Pro tier offers 20M characters, Business tier 50M characters, and Enterprise offers unlimited. Users can upload documents to create a knowledge base that agents reference when answering queries. Voice agents use the same knowledge base as text-based agents for consistent cross-channel responses.
ai_and_rag_capabilities.agent_capabilities: multi-step | multi-agent | autonomous. Lindy agents can perform multi-step workflows with triggers, conditions, and branching actions. Agents can call other agents (agent-to-agent delegation). Computer Use enables autonomous web browsing and interaction. Gaia voice agents handle multi-turn dialogues with context awareness and human handoff capabilities. Agents can autonomously update CRM systems, send follow-ups, qualify leads, and route complex issues.
ai_and_rag_capabilities.model_selection: Multi-vendor. Users can choose between Anthropic (Claude Sonnet 4.5, 3.7, Haiku 3.5), OpenAI (GPT-5, GPT-5 Codex), and Google (Gemini Flash 2.0) models. Model selection can be configured per agent.
ai_and_rag_capabilities.prompt_management: Built-in prompt configuration with natural language instructions. Lindy Academy includes an AI Agent Prompt Guide for crafting effective prompts. Users define agent behavior, persona, and instructions through prompts. The platform provides prompt templates for common use cases.

integration_and_ecosystem.key_integrations: Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack, HubSpot, Salesforce, Zoom, Twilio, Notion, Airtable, Microsoft 365, LinkedIn, Stripe, Shopify, Zendesk, Intercom, Discord, WhatsApp, and thousands more. HTTP Request action enables arbitrary API integration with custom methods, headers, and JSON bodies.
integration_and_ecosystem.integration_count: 4,000-5,000+ integrations (sources vary between 4,000+ and 5,000+ business integrations). Free tier provides access to 100+ integrations; Pro and above unlock 4,000+.
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_support: Not yet. As of mid-2025, Lindy is not formally compatible with Model Context Protocol (MCP), though its architecture naturally aligns with MCP principles for modular agent collaboration. Formal MCP support may come in future updates.
integration_and_ecosystem.webhook_support: Yes. Full webhook trigger support with unique URLs and security settings per webhook. Incoming webhook data can be processed by AI agents using natural language prompts or direct data referencing. Supports combining webhook triggers with AI Agent steps for intelligent data processing and downstream API calls.
integration_and_ecosystem.export_formats: Embeddable web chat widget (popup or iFrame via Lindy Embed), customizable branding (display name, accent color, domain restriction), WordPress and Squarespace integration via code injection. No standalone app export or code export documented. Primary deployment is cloud-based with embed and API access.

pricing_and_accessibility.pricing_model: freemium + subscription + credit-based. Four tiers (Free, Pro, Business, Enterprise) with credit-based consumption. Additional credits available at $10 per 1,000 credits. Simple workflows consume 1-3 credits; complex multi-step automations or large LLM tasks consume 10+ credits.
pricing_and_accessibility.free_tier_limits: Free plan: $0/month, 400 credits/month, up to 40 tasks, 1M character knowledge base, access to 100+ integrations, core features including Agent Builder, Lindy Build. No phone calls included. Suitable for learning and basic prototyping.
pricing_and_accessibility.paid_plans: Pro: $29.99/month, 3,000 credits, up to 1,500 tasks, 30 calls/month, 20M character knowledge base, 4,000+ integrations, 1 concurrent call, English-only voice, team members $19.99/month each, Lindy branding included. Business: $199.99/month, 20,000 credits, all Pro features, unlimited phone calls, 30+ supported languages, 50M character knowledge base, unlimited concurrent calls, call transfers, custom phone numbers, team members $19.99/month each. Enterprise: custom pricing, all Business features, enterprise-grade security, dedicated AI engineer, volume-based credit discounts, unlimited knowledge base, priority support, unlimited phone numbers and concurrent calls.
pricing_and_accessibility.open_source: No (proprietary). Lindy is a fully closed-source proprietary SaaS platform.
pricing_and_accessibility.self_hosting_option: Not available. Lindy is cloud-only SaaS with no self-hosting option.
pricing_and_accessibility.data_residency_and_sovereignty: SOC 2 Type II certified (audited by independent auditors, verified by Drata). HIPAA compliant. GDPR compliant. PIPEDA compliant. Data encrypted with TLS 1.2+ in transit and AES-256 at rest. Two-factor authentication available for all accounts. SSO and SAML support on higher plans. Personal data never used to train generative AI models. No explicit EU-specific data residency option documented. Trust Center available via Drata partnership.

adoption_and_market.market_position: Emerging leader in the AI-first no-code automation category. Lindy positions itself as the 'Zapier of AI,' differentiating from traditional automation tools by using LLMs for context-aware decision-making rather than rigid if-then rules. Rapidly growing with strong product-market fit since May 2024. Rated 4.9/5 on G2 from 170+ verified reviews.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: Primarily SMBs, startups, and growth-stage companies. Case studies include: Interlaced (meeting-to-CRM data automation), Blackbird (sales motion automation), Seven Zero Ventures (partner program scaling), VC CFO (automated valuation memos), Dr. Audrey Pinette's clinic (healthcare workflow automation), The Sauna Place (revenue recovery). One SaaS startup uses Lindy to book 40+ meetings monthly via automated lead outreach. A bootstrapped productivity tool resolves 70%+ of support tickets with Lindy AI agents.
adoption_and_market.community_size: 170+ G2 reviews (4.9/5 rating). 37-50 employees (2024-2025). 70,000 waitlist signups from initial demo video in March 2023. Lindy Academy and Documentation available for user education. Exact registered user count not publicly disclosed. [uncertain]
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: Total funding: ~$50M across multiple rounds. Series B: $35M (January 2023, led by Battery Ventures, Coatue, Menlo Ventures). Additional investors include Instacart co-founder Max Mullen. Revenue: $5.1M as of October 2024 (37-person team). Hit product-market fit in May 2024 and grew to 'high 7-figures' ARR. Note: some funding may include capital raised under the prior entity TeamFlow. [uncertain]
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Main competitors: Zapier (simple rule-based automation, 7,000+ apps, more integrations but no AI agents), Make/Integromat (visual automation, flexible but requires more setup), n8n (open-source, developer-focused, self-hostable, strong data privacy), Relevance AI (AI agent platform, more enterprise-focused), Gumloop (AI automation alternative), Voiceflow (conversational AI focus), Bland AI and Vapi (voice-specific competitors). Lindy differentiates through: (1) AI-native approach with LLM-powered agents vs. rigid automation, (2) Computer Use for apps without APIs, (3) combined text/voice/web channels, (4) natural language agent creation, (5) fast time-to-value with 1,000+ templates.
adoption_and_market.ecosystem_lock_in_risk: high. Lindy is fully proprietary with no open-source components, no code export, and no self-hosting option. Agent logic and workflows are stored in Lindy's cloud with no documented portability to competing platforms. Knowledge base content and integrations are platform-specific. Credit-based pricing creates usage dependency. If Lindy changes pricing or discontinues service, migration would require rebuilding all agents from scratch on another platform.

teaching_and_classroom.class_project_idea:
Project 1: 'AI Email Assistant for a Startup' (45 min) - Students sign up for Lindy's free tier (400 credits), use the Getting Started 101 template to build an AI email assistant that automatically triages incoming emails, drafts responses for common inquiries, and flags urgent messages. They configure the agent's persona and instructions, connect it to a test Gmail account, and test with sample emails. Deliverable: working email assistant demo + 2-slide analysis of time savings and cost per automated email vs. human processing.

Project 2: 'Lead Qualification AI Agent with CRM Integration' (75 min) - Students build a multi-step AI agent that receives leads via webhook (simulating a website form), qualifies them through predefined criteria (company size, budget, timeline), scores the lead, and routes qualified leads to a simulated CRM entry. Students use Lindy's visual workflow builder to define triggers, conditions, and actions. They compare Lindy's AI-native approach (contextual decision-making) to traditional Zapier-style automation (rigid rules). Deliverable: working agent demo + comparison table of AI-native vs. rule-based automation approaches with cost-benefit analysis.

teaching_and_classroom.student_prerequisites: nothing. Lindy is designed for non-technical users. Agent creation uses natural language descriptions. The visual builder requires no coding knowledge. Basic familiarity with email and business workflows is helpful but not required.
teaching_and_classroom.session_mapping: Session 2 (Prompt Engineering & No-Code Tools) - primary fit. Students use Lindy to build working AI agents, applying prompt engineering concepts through the natural language agent builder. Also relevant to Session 3 (Framing & Managing AI Projects) for Build vs Buy discussions comparing AI-native automation to traditional tools, and Session 4 (AI Business Models) for analyzing automation-as-a-service unit economics and credit-based pricing models.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Lindy is ideal for pre-seed to Series A startups with 1-15 person teams who need to automate repetitive knowledge work without hiring developers. Best suited for: (1) Sales automation - lead qualification, outbound email personalization, CRM updates from meeting transcripts (one startup books 40+ meetings/month with Lindy); (2) Customer support - AI agents that resolve 70%+ of routine tickets and route complex issues to humans; (3) Operations - meeting note automation, email triage, data entry, invoice processing; (4) Voice interactions - phone-based lead qualification, appointment scheduling, customer service via Gaia. The free tier (400 credits/month) is sufficient for prototyping and validating one use case. Teams should graduate to Pro ($29.99/month) for production use with 1,500 tasks/month. Lindy is particularly valuable when the founding team wants AI-powered automation beyond what Zapier offers but cannot afford to build custom AI pipelines.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_mvp: Minutes to hours for basic agents (email assistant, meeting summarizer). 1-3 days for multi-step production workflows with integrations, knowledge base, and webhook triggers. Lindy claims 'prompt to agent in 60 seconds,' and the Getting Started 101 tutorial shows a working email assistant in under 5 minutes. Complex multi-agent systems with Computer Use and voice agents may take 1-2 weeks to properly configure and test.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Use Lindy when: your team lacks AI engineering expertise, you need to automate knowledge work quickly, your use cases fit standard patterns (email, CRM, support, meetings), you want multi-channel automation (text + voice + web), or you need to validate an automation idea before investing in custom development. Build custom when: you need full control over AI model behavior and prompts, your data sensitivity requires self-hosting, you have high-volume workflows where credit costs exceed custom development costs, or you need deep integration with proprietary internal systems. Consider alternatives: n8n for self-hosting and open-source (better data sovereignty), Zapier for simple integrations without AI needs, Voiceflow for complex conversational design, or Relevance AI for enterprise-grade agent orchestration. Cost comparison: Lindy Pro at $29.99/month is significantly cheaper than Voiceflow Pro ($60/month) and competitive with Zapier Professional ($29.99/month), but credit consumption for AI-heavy workflows can escalate costs unpredictably.
key_lessons: 1. AI-native automation is a paradigm shift: Lindy demonstrates how LLM-powered agents differ fundamentally from rule-based automation (Zapier/Make). Instead of mapping every possible scenario with if-then rules, AI agents handle ambiguity and edge cases contextually. Entrepreneurs should evaluate whether their automation needs require judgment (use Lindy) or pure data routing (use Zapier).

2. Start with one high-impact workflow: The most successful Lindy users start by automating a single painful workflow (e.g., meeting notes to CRM, email triage, lead qualification) rather than trying to automate everything at once. Measure the time saved and cost per automated task before expanding.

3. Credit economics matter at scale: Simple workflows cost 1-3 credits, but complex multi-step AI tasks can consume 10+ credits each. Model your unit economics carefully: at $10 per 1,000 credits, a workflow consuming 10 credits costs $0.10 per execution. Compare this to the hourly cost of the manual task to ensure positive ROI.

4. Computer Use unlocks the long tail of automation: Many business tools lack APIs, making them impossible to automate with traditional platforms. Lindy's Computer Use feature can interact with any web application, opening automation possibilities for legacy software, niche SaaS tools, and web-based processes that competitors cannot touch.

5. Lock-in is the tradeoff for speed: Lindy's ease of use comes at the cost of portability. All agent logic, knowledge bases, and workflows are proprietary and non-exportable. Document your automation logic externally and plan for the possibility of rebuilding on another platform if Lindy's pricing or features change.

The distinction between 4,000+ and 5,000+ integrations varies across sources and may reflect rapid growth or different counting methodologies. Funding totals (~$50M) may partially include capital raised under the prior entity TeamFlow before the pivot to Lindy. MCP support status is based on mid-2025 data and may have changed. AI model availability (GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4.5) reflects late 2025 updates and will continue evolving. Enterprise pricing and features are not publicly documented and require sales contact. The platform is evolving rapidly with significant updates (v3.0 in August 2025), so features and pricing may change.
